latency_protocol: fresh CLI process per query, spawn through exit, no warmup; p95 nearest rank

rows.query: Our API starts returning 429 after repeated calls. Where are the request counter and waiting period checked before letting another call through?
Why can an emailed password recovery link be rejected when it is old, and what prevents using the same link again after a successful change?
Where is a deleted record brought back by clearing its deletion date, including the option for an event listener to cancel the operation?
When the database reports a deadlock, where is the decision made to retry the whole transaction or give up after the allowed attempts?
A user can still sign in with a password stored using our old hashing settings. Where does a successful check cause the saved hash to be upgraded?
I want an email task to run only after database work succeeds, and never if it rolls back. Where are those deferred callbacks registered and later run or discarded?
A form submitted over HTTPS is rejected even though its token looks valid. Where are the browser origin and referring address checked before the form can reach the view?
Where does the upload pipeline decide whether to hold incoming file bytes in memory or let a temporary disk file handle a larger upload?
A template needs a value from the process environment but access is denied. Where does the template call reach the policy that decides which variable names are allowed?
After renaming a page, how are its old addresses turned into small HTML pages that send visitors to the new address?
Where is a long collection of articles divided into numbered result pages, including the behavior when the collection is empty?
Which code keeps unpublished drafts, articles scheduled for a later date, and expired articles out of the generated site unless their inclusion is requested?

score_protocol: all scheduled rows retained; positive-label errors score zero; empty labels have separate no-answer score; partial responses score delivered hits and fail the run
